object_wins.rule: Strict per-object comparison results[obj]['GRUctx|lag3']['seg_f1'] > results[obj]['SF|lag3']['seg_f1'] over the 17 keys of 'objects' (not episode rows): 17/17 in CRPS_L2_EVAL.json. The same rule in CRPS_L2_ALGO_ROUND.json gives 15/17 (D-SUB -0.0211, medium gear -0.0116), so the report's 17/17 holds only for the main L2 file.

episode_claim.why: Flattening all episode_paired rows gives 1464 rows but only 111 unique episode ids (each episode appears in ~13.2 object folds); averaging each episode's dSegF1 over its folds gives 97 positive and 14 negative in CRPS_L2_EVAL.json, not 96/15. The audit's own per-date signs sum to 96 only because it records 26/34 on 2025-01-13 where the data give 27/34.

strongest_deployable_baseline.why_the_others_are_not_eligible: SFA_Oracle (0.8236) needs the true parent action at every frame and Shufctx (0.4098) is a shuffled-context control, so neither is deployable; GateCtx (0.7093) and GRUctx (0.7091) are the champion family, and GRUskill (0.6514)/DualHead (0.6468) are deployable but weaker than SF.

does_not_license: These DEV-only numbers from 17 correlated leave-one-object folds (mean pairwise test overlap 75.8 of 86.1 episodes) do not license any claim about truly unseen objects, the untouched 37-episode sealed cross-recording set (G1), or state-of-the-art/deployment performance.
method:
Per-object macro = unweighted mean over the 17 'objects' of results[obj][scheme]['seg_f1'] (CRPS_L2_ALGO_ROUND.json for the round table; CRPS_L2_EVAL.json recomputed separately: SF 0.671750, GRUctx 0.713501).
Object wins = strict '>' at object level, counted once per object, both files.
Episode claim = results[obj]['episode_paired'] flattened, deduped to 111 unique episode ids, dSegF1 averaged within episode across folds, then counted mean>0; sanity checks gave mean per-episode dSegF1 0.04461 (report 0.0447).
Cross-checks: test-set size 86.1 and mean pairwise overlap 75.8 reproduce the audit exactly; boundary F1 means 0.59484 (SF) / 0.58945 (GRUctx) reproduce the report, not the audit's 0.5954/0.5901.
No number was taken from the report or the audit; all were recomputed from the two result JSONs.
